answer: Each agent earns a reputation token on a ridge‑scaled ledger, where the token’s value grows linearly with the node’s age and drops to zero if the agent is idle for more than a basalt‑defined epoch. When a new identity is created it must stake a jade‑priced bond equal to the current reputation of the oldest trusted node, lock it for one ridge period, and prove continuous activity to avoid automatic decay. An attacker therefore pays a per‑identity cost of the full jade bond plus the waiting time of one ridge epoch, making large‑scale Sybil attacks financially prohibitive.
